# Power and Politics

*Pages PDF 25-29*

Dark elves further down the ark’s hierarchy are much the same. Each carves out their own niche in the black ark’s society and endeavours to protect themselves from others, both physically and politically. They form alliances of convenience and cooperate until it no longer serves their purpose. While some may tire of constant vigilance and mistrust, they know that this is the lot of the Druchii. 

## **Power and Politics**
Duriath Helbane is the fleetmaster of _Temple of Spite_ , by order of the rulers of Clar Karond and the patronage of Malerion. Provided he pleases Malerion, Lord Venil Chillwind (whilst plundering the seas east of Naggaroth), and Lady Drane Brackblood (whilst plundering to the west), Helbane inherits absolute authority. His position is protected by Anethra Helbane, a close ally of Morathi. She protects Duriath from his enemies in Naggaroth so long as it suits her purposes. 

Two events loom large over life on the ark. Scars from the failed mutiny are barely healed, potential mutineers survive, but live in fear that their prior allegiance is known to others. Overshadowing life for all dark elves is the all-pervading influence of Malerion, personified by his envoy, Myrrhven Silkblood. The Druchii of _Temple of Spite_ believe his eye is on their every deed, vigilant for any sign of disloyalty or weakness. 

Duriath convenes two councils as he sees fit. They can advise and advocate for their position, but have no say over his actions, and must swear fealty to the fleetmaster each year at the Bearing of Chains ceremony. 

## **The Council of Reavers**
## **The Dread King’s Emissary**
The Council of Reavers is an assembly of corsair captains representing the fleet. They play an important role in bringing wealth to the black ark from raids, defending it from attack, and hunting other ships. Each captain must bring tribute to Helbane, but otherwise they can operate with independence. 

Myrrhven Silkblood is unpopular amongst the ark’s powerful. he is rumoured to conceal an iron writ from malerion, permitting him to take command of _Temple of Spite_ should he see fit. He has not confirmed or denied these rumours, as they serve his purpose well. Silkblood schemes to trap other powerful Druchii into proving their disloyalty to Malerion. He does this to diminish threats to his master and because he enjoys inflicting psychological distress. 

## **The Black Convocation**
The Black Convocation comprises representatives of the ark’s various factions and Naggarothi interests. Delegates include the Death Hag Kheitalla, Supreme Sorceress Xalthia, Master Tualarc of the warhost, Storm Witch Neryssa, High Beastmaster Scaleflayer, castellans Lady Hawkbane and Lord Skaris, a handful of favoured corsair captains, and Lord Myrrhven Silkblood, emissary of Malerion. 

Silkblood thinks escaped captives or stowaways offer delicious possibilities. If they serve a purpose in his schemes, the Characters may find him to be their best protection. 

## **Nobility at Sea**
Beneath the two councils are the highborn, dark elf nobles posted to _Temple of Spite_ . Some have hereditary connections to the ark, their lineages long resident in the towers of the Fleetmaster’s Bastion or the Vanguard Spires. Others are aboard for their own purposes, to travel the ocean for political or other reasons. Intrigue between these highborn is endemic, and there is little mutual trust, as each noble sees themself as either predator or prey. They post guards around their chambers and hire spies and informers to gather intelligence on their rivals’ movements and plans. Druchii highborn have their own eccentric pursuits, with which they keep themselves entertained. For example, Lady Noctra Sorrowsharp cultivates a small flock of razorbills, trained to attack people on deck when it amuses her. Lady Karasashalla enjoys blackmail and sending poison pen letters, sometimes literally laced with black lotus. 

## **Fleets and Corsairs**
The captains of Helbane’s fleet are rivalled only by the sorceresses for power and influence. Vicious corsairs who venture forth to plunder the world and bring spoils back to Naggaroth, they extend the reach of the ark and Malerion alike. 

Fleetmaster Helbane favours the Council of Reavers over the Black Convocation. He comes from their ranks and respects their role and experience, but he rules them with a capricious whim. 

Favoured captains can enjoy power and influence for many years before the fleetmaster or his peers engineer their fall from grace, such was the case with Captain Mancleaver, who was a favourite of Helbane until rumours were spread that he planned to mutiny. Now, tattered remnants of the captain’s skin flap from a flagstaff atop the Chain Spire. 

Individual captains’ position in the hierarchy comes from their achievements rather than the size of their command. Some of them captain a single, blood-soaked vessel and yet stand high in esteem, their reputations forged through audacity and slaughter, while others lead entire squadrons only so long as their victories continue to justify their authority. _Temple of Spite_ ’s fleet currently consists of several raiding and scouting flotilla, composed mainly of ravenships with waveblades and doomreaver support. Many smaller vessels and sea chariots carry important personages, while wrackhold transport vessels carry cargo or troops as required. 

## **Notable Reavers**
Fourteen captains sit on the Reavers’ Council. The following are notorious amongst the population of the ark for their exploits and larger-than-life personalities. 

- **Captain Arheth Flariel** is renowned for his independent, swashbuckling spirit. Helbane finds Flariel amusing and enterprising, so allows him to sail the _Raptor’s Talon_ where he likes. See _**The Corsairs of Captain Flariel**_ . 

- **Captain Qulla Darkfaith** is exacting and impeccable, Qulla commands with the precision of an elf who insists her dragonskin cloak is polished to a shine. She leads a squadron of ravenships from her personal command, the _Crimson Scourge_ . 

- **Captain Malida Redthorn** is often disparaged by other corsairs as ‘Xalthia’s creature’, Redthorn and her corsairs are closely affiliated with the ark’s sorceress coven. Her crew is often accompanied by one of the sorceresses, weaving illusions to conceal her ravenships and the death fortress she commands. 

- **Captain Nyandra Filvanir,** whose ship _Nightwake_ heralds trade or death. Filvanir is a merchant corsair always looking for profit. See page 106. 

- **Captain Yrmaldrel Manbane** is a close ally of the high beastmaster. Manbane oversees the fleet’s doomreavers. He and his crew are enthusiastic hunters of sea monsters. 

- **Captain Vaelen Frosthand** is a stickler for tradition. Frosthand sails the _Hound of Drakhira_ , a venerable storm barque accompanied by his son Heiron’s ravenship. 

- **Captain Maelrin Wavebane** is an especially bloodthirsty reaver captain, with a ferocious temper and an especially belligerent crew of corsairs. 

Other corsairs crew the ark itself, rather than sail with the fleet. These companies are responsible for defending the ark from seaborne attacks and ordering dark elf sailors and captives to perform the mundane tasks they consider beneath them. Druchii sailors are expert mariners, though less accomplished than their Asur counterparts, their skill undermined by lacklustre teamwork. 

Corsairs walk the ark with a swaggering confidence, sneering their superiority at servants, menials, and even members of the warhost. When ships are berthed in the inner docks, they bunk in several raider lodges on the ark, which are known to be raucous places by dark elf standards. Corsairs have their own rituals and traditions, part of a maritime subculture alien to land-dwelling Druchii. They pay special heed to Mathlann, though they rarely invoke his name, preferring to swear to the ‘dragons below’, the Lord of the Seas’ offspring who determine the fate of all who venture onto the waves. 

## **Corsairs and Soldiers**
There is rivalry between corsairs and the regiments of the warhost. Violence is common enough that Master Tualarc insists his troops stay away from the raider lodges, especially as reavers have the upper hand. Helbane is unconcerned, as his favoured corsairs usually prevail and conflict winnows out the weak. Likewise, ships compete with one another for reputation and fame. The most impressive exploits involve humiliation or slaughter of the hated sea elves, who the corsairs regard as bitter rivals in seamanship as well as minions of the phoenix king. 

## **The Sorceresses’ Coven**
_Temple of Spite_ ’s coven is an extension of the Dark Convent of Ghrond and consists of a gathering of sorceresses that exact the will of Anethra Helbane and Morathi across the world. They wield extensive power on board, both literal and political, as the ark depends on their sorceries to stalk the oceans. 

## **Supreme Sorceress Nightwind**
Supreme Sorceress Xalthea Nightwind was Anethra Helbane’s apprentice and represents the coven on the Black Convocation. Duriath and Nightwind find themselves in alliance on most matters, but their arrangements are borne of pragmatism rather than mutual trust. She is a gaunt, humourless elf who supposedly never sleeps and obsesses over a task demanded of her by Anethra Helbane, to seek out a set of powerful crystalline artefacts forged by the dwarfs before the War of the Beard, known to scholars of magic as the ‘doomstones’. 

## **Other Resident Sorceresses**
Other than Xalthea, there are five other sorceresses resident on the ark, while others travel on board on their own affairs: 

- **Saerith the Bladed** is bonded to _Temple of Spite_ . She tends to the physical and mystical substance of the ark. Saerith has become distracted of late; she is a secret Slaaneshi cultist and occasional bedmate of Duriath Helbane. 

- **Samuril** is a restless soul, preoccupied with conquest and exploration. She travels with Khaine’s Eyes (see page 91) and the other sorceresses resent her frequent absences. 

- **Rakaria Dran** chose to escape the paranoia and politics of Ghrond to study the history of elves across the world. See _**The Corsairs of Captain Flariel**_ . 

- **Mortella** is addicted to deceit. She toys with illusion, and at any time her chambers may appear as an arboretum of rare trees, an icy waste, or a lush jungle. Mortella is an enthusiastic follower of Slaanesh, and more adept than Saerith at keeping this secret. 

- **Netathi Fellwhisper** is withdrawn and an outsider amongst her sisters. She strives to emulate Morathi and Malerion in understanding the ways of daemons and dark entities, hoping to master them in exchange for power. 

The sorceresses are attended by acolytes and aspirants, who hope to learn from their betters and one day ascend to the Dark Convent of Ghrond themselves. 

## **The Warhost**
The dark elf warriors stationed on _Temple of Spite_ are an army in formation. Helbane and Lord Tualarc agree they lack a sufficient muster to take Tor Elithis, however, and it is paramount that they attract the support of Naggarothi lords to augment their forces. Lord Tualarc is an old campaigner who harbours a longstanding frustration that his many victories have yet to see him elevated to become a dreadlord. He sees the conquest of Tor Elithis as a way to right that wrong. 

The army is billeted throughout the ark in warrior halls. They must serve guard duty, patrolling the halls and decks to keep the inhabitants in line and quell discord. Tualarc insists his warhost live an austere, disciplined life, drawing on his experience commanding the northern watchtower of Shagrath on the border of the Chaos Wastes. The strict military culture amongst the warriors contrasts with the swaggering arrogance and rakish lifestyle of the corsairs, and there is no love lost between the reavers and the warriors. 

The majority of warriors fight as spearmen, repeater crossbowmen, and swordsmen, along with a contingent of dark riders, Shades and a company of cold one knights. In a pitched battle, the Council of Reavers would send corsairs and the Khainites their own bloodthirsty fighters, although there are too few of the temple’s executioner contingent to form a regiment. Malerion has yet to declare explicit support for Helbane’s ambitions. Should that happen, the warhost will expand and may even secure the support of the Black Guard of Naggaroth. 

Helbane sponsors the Tidepiercers, the Spears of the Drowned Moon, and Valerion’s Blackswords (see page 69). They receive additional pay, extra privileges, and superior equipment. Having proven their loyalty against mutineers in the attempted coup, Helbane has come to rely on them for security. 

## **Devotees of Khaine**
All dark elves honour Khaine, but there are some whose devotion borders on fanaticism. The Khainites resident on _Temple of Spite_ wish to slaughter across the world in the name of the Lord of Murder. They reside in Valeth’s Palace, literally and spiritually close to the temple of Khaine and the presiding death hag Kheitalla and her witch elves. 

What the Khainite faction lacks in numbers, they make up for in single-minded zealotry. They are inflexible and reluctant to bow to Helbane or any authority other than their god, and when they feel disrespected or compromised, they often murder their way out of the situation. Fortunately for the other inhabitants, this leaves them isolated and they struggle to form alliances with other factions, which keeps their worst tendencies in check. 

The temple of Khaine takes a tithe of all captives for sacrifice, and demands that any captured wizard is immediately slain in the name of their god. The sorceresses resent this, as they have other uses for imprisoned spellcasters. For more detail on the Khainites, see page 112. 

## **Beasts and Their Masters**
_Temple of Spite_ plays host to a wide variety of fearsome creatures, and its surrounding waters roil with twisting backs and thrashing tendrils. Hydras, cold ones, manticores, even a kharibdyss live restrained within the vaults beneath the waterline. From their cages and pits, the screams of their meals rise to the Temple of Anath Raema, placating the goddess until the dark elves make landfall and a true hunt can begin. 

Beastmasters from Clar Karond oversee _Temple of Spite_ ’s creatures and its ever-growing horde of captives. They work tirelessly to ensure the beasts are fit and ready to fight, though this is not their only purpose. 

Their lords in Clar Karond seek new monsters for their collections, which is a mission the beastmasters relish, and they are constantly on the lookout for strange and deadly new beasts. Whenever the ark approaches land, the beastmasters head out, seeking new beasts and captives to trap and drag away. 

Scorath Coldblood is high beastmaster, and despite his youth, he has a reputation as a skilled and ruthless handler, said to command even hydra with nothing more than a glare. The lords of Clar Karond assigned him command of their contingent aboard the _Temple of Spite_ in recognition of his talent. This should be a position of great honour, which grants a place on the Black Convocation, but in practice, Scorath and his beastmasters are treated with indifference. They are seen as jumped-up stable hands by highborn Druchii and other powerful figures, and only a handful of dark elves treat them with due respect.  It is a situation Scorath loathes with all his being. 

## **Civilians and Captives**
More than just a warship, _Temple of Spite_ is a city afloat, with a feudal society mirroring life in Naggaroth. Civilians serve in tightly-defined roles, as household servants, overseers, traders, and artisans. Despite the cruelty inherent to Druchii culture, most live in relative comfort, providing they watch their back and please their masters. 

Merchants and artisans maintain a thriving, if grim, economy. Most trade supplies goods and services to the inhabitants of the ark, though a select few merchants conduct business with those ports around the world willing to entertain Druchii trade. Currency takes the form of silver coins stamped with twin moons and the rune of Malerion. Wealth from raids and foreign trade is exchanged by the purser Selkar Khaevrin from his counting house in the Fleetmasters’ Bastion. 

Many dark elves aboard are servants of the highborn or other powerful figures. They ensure the smooth running of noble households, supervise captive labour, and manage their masters’ affairs. Survival in such a role requires a deft combination of discretion, competence, and the ability to anticipate the whims of their betters. Those who fail quickly find themselves demoted from their posts, assuming they are lucky enough to escape being used as bloody sacrifice. 

At the bottom of society are the captives. Most are exploited for labour on the ark, while others are destined for the cities of Naggaroth or sacrifice to the gods. These unfortunates endure horrific conditions, their lives too often short and brutal. Dwarfs are especially prized: resilient and skilled, their pride means they struggle to overcome their reluctance to craft fine goods for their captors. 

High and wood elves are prized as valuable trophies, frequently tormented, offered to dark gods, or used to provide entertainment. Humans make up most of the captives, drawn from many nations. There are also captive orcs and beastmen, used in the fighting pits or as heavy labour, though their unruly nature makes them difficult to keep. 

## **The Cult of Slaanesh**
Malerion forbids the worship of Slaanesh, yet elves have always been susceptible to the allure of the Dark Prince. Cults of Pleasure persist throughout Naggaroth, meeting in the shadows for their debauched ceremonies, hidden from Malerion’s agents and the vigilance of the Khainites, who hold Slaanesh’s followers in special contempt. Some whisper that Morathi retains a hold over the cults of pleasure, having never truly relinquished them. 

A cult of Slaanesh worships in secret on _Temple of Spite_ , deep below the waterline in a temple dating back to Nagarythe’s original pleasure cults. The cave is carved with six levels of terracing beneath an altar marked with the god’s sigil. Behind the altar, a curtained arch leads to the scented throneroom of the Anointed, where the sacred figurehead of the cult holds court. Nzandra the Tormentor is an ancient champion of the Dark Prince, her mind scarred irreparably after millennia of servitude to her rapacious god. 

## **The Exalted Seekers**
An inner circle of six ‘Exalted Seekers’ sit below Nzandra in the cult hierarchy, each a highborn who keeps their identity secret. 

The cult are in awe of Nzandra, a living vessel of their god’s will. They are also terrified. Her face has an unsettling beauty, she can move at preternatural speed, and she emits a mildly hallucinogenic aura that instills exquisitely disturbing dreams for many weeks after exposure. Her presence is addictive and spiritually draining, so even if the inner circle wanted to leave the cult, they would find it all but impossible. For her part, Nzandra grows bored of dwelling in her perfumed sanctuary, no matter how luxurious. She longs to stalk the decks and towers of the black ark, taking pleasure wherever and however she chooses. The Exalted Seekers encourage her to remain within the depths, believing it would lead to their exposure otherwise, but Nzandra finds the prospect of exploration perversely tantalising. 

Despite their caution, the cult’s existence is an open secret on _Temple of Spite_ . Dark elves make subtle allusions to the cult in their conversation and frequently insinuate a rival is amongst their number. The Cult of Khaine works to uncover the inner circle and discover the temple, to eradicate those who defy Malerion and vaunt Slaanesh over Khaine. 

Morathi herself told Saerith that Nzandra must not be discovered, on pain of death. The sorceress coven believes the Dark Mother may have plans for the Anointed. 

- **Saerith the Bladed** , sorceress 

- **Maldrel Blackcrown** , lordling in the warhost 

- **Captain Vaelen Frosthand** , commander of the _Hound of Drakhira_ raiding ship 

- **Mortella** , sorceress 

- **Lady Akria Spitemoon** , highborn 

- **Lord Kranach Meurlith** , highborn 

Each Exalted Seeker leads the worship of six acolytes. The wider cult includes Druchii from all levels of society on _Temple of Spite_ . Some are recruited from the ranks of dark elves with a particular affinity for Atharti, as they are deemed susceptible to the lure of Slaanesh. Cultists wear masks of exquisite craftsmanship in the temple, fashioned with the leering faces of daemonettes and weirder creatures of Slaanesh. Despite these disguises and the care with which worshippers cover their tracks, the population of the ark is not large, and most cultists could identify their fellow worshippers by voice, or other distinguishing characteristics, if they were inclined.
